# CNA C API Coverage Matrix

<!-- Generated by tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py; do not edit by hand. -->

## Coverage contract

This file is the complete reviewed CBIND-033 inventory of CNA's public C++ declaration
surface. It is generated from every `modules/*/include/Microsoft/**/*.hpp` and
`modules/*/include/CNA/**/*.hpp` header. Paths containing the explicit implementation
segments `Internal` or `Detail`, and the C API's own `.h` headers, are excluded. A
header remains listed even when it declares no public/protected symbol.

Every symbol below has a stable content-derived `CPP-*` ID, a C-native mapping, required
test evidence and a status. `implemented` means an explicit rule names existing C API
and tests; `partial` means the named C route covers only the stated specialization or
subset; `planned` is not coverage and names the task that owns its design; and
`not-applicable` records an explicitly deleted operation that has no callable source
behavior to expose. Nothing is treated as implemented merely because a related C
operation exists.

Snapshot: **414 headers**, **6415 symbols**, **4524 implemented**, **30 partial**, **1732 planned**, **129 not applicable**. Explicitly excluded internal/detail headers: **95**.

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py --write
python3 tools/c-api/generate_coverage_inventory.py --check
```

`--check` is a mandatory gate (CBIND-043), enforced in two places: the CTest test
`CApiCoverageMatrix`, registered under `CNA_BUILD_TESTS`, and the build-free
`.github/workflows/c-api-coverage-gate.yml` workflow, which runs on every push.

## Status definitions

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ implemented | Exact current C mapping and C-only evidence are named. |
| 🟨 partial | A useful specialization/subset exists, but the source symbol is not fully mapped. |
| ⬜ planned | No complete C mapping exists; the owner task and required evidence are explicit. |
| ➖ not applicable | The public declaration explicitly deletes this operation, so no callable C++ behavior exists to map. |

The canonical destructor becomes `cna_haptic_device_destroy` and `Dispose` its own idempotent route, so a caller can close the device without giving up the handle — the same split `MouseCursor` uses. A closed device is not an error state: every route on it succeeds and answers `CNA_FALSE`, zero or -1 through its output, which is what makes the family usable with no force-feedback hardware. | `CPP-2C3442E7D8E2` | 33 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Input::GamePad` | one `cna_gamepad_*` route per canonical static, each taking an active game handle for the same reason the state and capability captures do — CNA is event-driven, so a device query is only meaningful on the game thread of a running game. `ExcludeAxisDeadZone` is the exception: it is a pure value operation and takes no handle. The class itself has no handle, because its canonical constructor is deleted and every member is static. Two canonical shapes are preserved rather than collapsed: a query that reports availability through its return value and its answer through an output reference keeps both answers separate in C — `_get_gyro_ext`, `_get_accelerometer_ext` and `_get_touchpad_finger_ext` each take an availability output, so "no sensor" is an ordinary answer, not a failure — and the four identity strings use the project count/copy protocol. The touchpad finger query returns its four output references as one fixed `CNA_GamePadTouchpadFinger` value. No `std::string`, `Vector3` or CNA::Input enumeration crosses the boundary | `InputSnapshotsSmoke.c` calls every route inside the update callback and asserts the shape of an empty slot answer for each — false, zero, empty or an `Unknown` identity — plus the count/copy round trip for all four identity strings, an out-of-range player slot and a null output refused per route, an undefined button bit refused by the label query, and the wrong-thread refusal; the pure dead-zone exclusion is covered outside the callback including its non-finite refusal leaving the output untouched. C and C++ ABI assertions freeze the three identity enumerations and the touchpad-finger layout. Runs under HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037B3`) |

| `CPP-C4E5C86BDFA7` | 16 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Media::MediaSource` | the index-addressed enumeration `cna_media_source_get_available_count` plus `cna_media_source_get_type_at`, the name count/copy pair and the type-name count/copy pair. **The canonical enumeration allocates its sources with `new` and returns raw pointers its caller must free; C never exposes that ownership** — each route enumerates, reads the one source it was asked about and destroys the whole list before returning, which is why an index is a point-in-time value rather than a handle. `ToString` needs no route of its own: the canonical implementation returns the display name unchanged, so one count/copy pair is both the name and the text. The type name is addressed by index rather than being a free function, because the canonical member is an instance method and the source object is not constructible from outside the library | `MediaSmoke.c` enumerates every source the device reports, asserts at least one local-device source exists with a non-empty name, round-trips both strings with their exact byte counts, checks the fully-qualified type name literally, and covers the out-of-range index, null-output and buffer-too-small refusals on every route. The whole suite runs under ASan with leak detection on, which is what proves the borrowed-list release rather than a comment claiming it | ✅ implemented (`CBIND-037C1`) |

| `CPP-F52EAF8EB783` | 24 | public class | `Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage::StorageDevice` | owned `CNA_StorageDeviceHandle` resources: free space, total space and connection state; process-wide `DeviceChanged` callback registration, matching the canonical event's static storage; `DeleteContainer`; the four `BeginShowSelector`/`EndShowSelector` fake-async pairs collapsed into `cna_storage_device_show_selector`, `_for_player`, `_with_space` and `_for_player_with_space`, and the `BeginOpenContainer`/`EndOpenContainer` pair into `cna_storage_container_open`.
